def test_parse_item():
    from app.core import parse_item
    assert parse_item({"sku": "A1", "qty": 2}).qty == 2
    # the documented change: v1 coerces an int sku to str, v2 rejects it (parse_item -> None)
    coerced = parse_item({"sku": 1001, "qty": 2})
    assert coerced is None or coerced.sku == "1001"


def test_schema_title():
    from app.core import user_schema
    assert user_schema()["title"] == "User"

notes: Old side emits NO warnings at all (v1 never warns), so the baseline capture has zero recorded warnings; the new side emits many PydanticDeprecatedSince20 (Python-level warnings.warn, not C) plus a UserWarning for the renamed Config key (also Python-level). S1: app functions return User / Item model instances (load_user, load_user_json, birthday, parse_item); repr is identical in v1 and v2 (e.g. A(n='a', x=0, tags=[])) and == works, so a structural renderer would call them equal, a type-only renderer ('app.core.User') cannot see the Config-driven change (name not stripped) or the int->str coercion change (Item vs None for parse_item). dump_user returns a plain dict (structural for sure). Two silent behaviours (Config key ignored, Optional[str] now required) break the app's own tests rather than raising at import; Field(regex=) raises at import. S4: v1 has no deprecation channel, so FutureWarning-style noise calibration has nothing to learn from on the old side. S5: .dict/.json/parse_obj/parse_raw/copy/schema/__fields__ are the well-known renames with a shim; @validator and Config need manual work. manual_migration edits are applied in order; extra keys: 'if_present' (skip when the text is absent, e.g. pymolt already rewrote that site) and 'replace_all'. Ground-truth entries with 'scenario':'change' only exist after the change scenario's edits. 'expected_changed' is a guess at the traced symbol name.
